subject: Mutual action schedule for CardioTech evaluation & environment wiring
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + action items: CardioTech evaluation environment

Alex — thanks for the productive demo yesterday. As discussed, I’m attaching a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) and a short checklist for environment wiring so we can lock the evaluation window and close timeline. High-level asks we need to complete before the evaluation starts:

- Org setup: create a service account/org unit we can use for evaluation (we need an org id and an admin contact).
- API keys: short-lived API key for staging (1-week TTL) + longer-lived test key for sustained runs.
- Network: add Redwood public egress IPs to your IP allowlist and confirm CIDR ranges you expect to peer.
- VPC peering: confirm whether you want route-exchange peering (preferred) or NAT-based access; provide VPC project IDs and owner contact.

Please review the attached MAP-draft-v1.pdf and the milestone sheet in the drive link I shared. Proposed evaluation kickoff: Apr 12 — gives engineering two full weeks to finish wiring. If that works, we’ll schedule a 30-minute technical handoff next week.

Next steps requested from CardioTech by Apr 5:
- Assign infra owner (email)
- Provide VPC project IDs and CIDR
- Confirm procurement cadence for test license/PO

I’m looping Neha for commercial cadence and Marissa for onboarding ops.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf
From: Alex Park <alex.park@cardiotech.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP + action items: CardioTech evaluation environment

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from infra/procurement side: we can assign an infra owner (I’ve CC’d ops+infra) and procurement will aim to turn around the evaluation PO within two weeks (depends on our vendor verification).

A couple of clarifying items:
- IP allowlist: we can update our firewall but will need the exact egress IPs and expected ports. Can you provide both ephemeral and static egress ranges?
- VPC peering: our network prefers route-exchange peering; I’ll pull project IDs and CIDRs and share by EOD Apr 2.
- API keys: procurement asked whether the short-lived key can be scoped to a specific model and rate-limited. That should be fine, yes?

I’ll follow up with concrete CIDRs and the infra owner once I’ve spoken to our network lead. Also open to the Apr 12 kickoff if the wiring is finished by then.

—Alex Park
Director, Platform Engineering | CardioTech

I’ve added this into HubSpot (HS-5873) and uploaded a quick milestone workbook (MAP-milestones-sheet.xlsx) to the shared drive. If the procurement PO takes longer than two weeks, let us know and we can offer a temporary hosted fallback while procurement completes.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@cardiotech.com>, ops+infra <ops+infra@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + action items: CardioTech evaluation environment

Alex / ops team — hi, Ben on the infra side. A few technical notes to speed the peering conversation:

- Preferred pattern: route-exchange peering with static routes announced from CardioTech to Redwood; this keeps latency low and avoids NAT.
- Ports: we need outbound 443 for model fetches and websocket/streaming on 443. No inbound ports required once peering is established.
- Egress IPs: we’ll provide a small set of stable IPs for your allowlist; ephemeral worker IPs are possible but require extra NAT rules.
- KMS/HSM: if you need integration with an on-prem KMS, we support HSM-backed key wrapping but that adds ~3 business days for key exchange and HSM attestation.

Action items for CardioTech: please send
- VPC project IDs and primary CIDR blocks
- Preferred peering model (route-exchange or NAT)
- Network contact for peering coordination (email + slack id)

I attached a tiny snippet with the peering template we use (peering-snippet.txt). Happy to hop on a short network call to walk through it.

—Ben Carter
Infra PM, Redwood Inference
Attachments: peering-snippet.txt
From: Alex Park <alex.park@cardiotech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + action items: CardioTech evaluation environment

Thanks Ben — quick follow-up from our network lead (copied in ops+infra):
- We prefer route-exchange peering.
- Primary CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16, project id: cardiotech-prod-vpc.
- Network contact: Priya Shen (priya.shen@cardiotech.com) — she’ll coordinate the peering ticket.
- IP allowlist: we can add up to five /32 entries; please provide the three stable egress IPs you referenced and confirm ports.

Regarding keys and KMS: procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a scoped test key limited to the evaluation model and a DocuSign statement of work. Procurement is also evaluating whether HSM key wrap is required; they’ll confirm by Apr 6.

Appreciate the offer to run a short network call — Priya, can we do 30 minutes Mon Apr 5 at 10am PT? If that works for Redwood, we’ll open the peering ticket after the call.

—Alex

Alex / Priya — great, that plan works. Confirming next steps and owners so we have a single source of truth in the MAP: 

- By Apr 5 (CardioTech): infra owner (Priya), VPC project id, CIDR (received), procurement confirmation on HSM (expected Apr 6).
- By Apr 7 (Redwood): provide three stable egress /32 IPs, scoped evaluation API key + rate limits, and the peering config template (I’ll attach MAP-final-draft.pdf after the call).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Karthik Iyer
